surat.headline: Severe yarn inflation and intensifying labor strikes strain Surat textiles despite diamond demand revival.
what_changed: Textile weaving units face potential early closure before Diwali driven by a ₹50/kg (reported up to 66%) surge in yarn prices.
Labor unrest escalated significantly with strikes, a 'Gaon Chalo' reverse migration exodus to UP/Bihar, and over 80 embroidery workers detained.
Credit discipline worsened via 70 blacklisted traders over ₹62 crore in dues, alongside a ₹10.14 crore textile fraud arrest.
The diamond segment showed mixed trends, shortening Diwali vacations on domestic demand while facing a 7% polished export shipment drop and UK LGD ad scrutiny.
stress_signals: Surat looms face early pre-Diwali closure due to a ₹50/kg yarn hike, alongside broader reports of a 66% yarn price surge squeezing unit margins [b567711c9ed4, b62552cc0c7d].

70 traders blacklisted for defaulting on ₹62 crore owed to viscose weavers, complemented by a ₹29.57 lakh Katargam grey fabric default and a ₹10.14 crore fraud arrest [a70c9ae52e8d, c4997bb35d98, 2514ad7d6e20].

Intense worker protests and strikes over wages and hours led to detention of 80+ embroidery workers, job exits, and migrant labor exodus to UP and Bihar [7697e96a190e, af8a29b318b7, d6a4b0e6a74b, 73dfcce5d3f4].
Polished diamond export shipments contracted by 7%, while UK authorities launched a crackdown on misleading lab-grown diamond advertisements [975918f112f3, b1b313249339].
improvement_signals: Diamond manufacturers shortened Diwali vacation duration for the first time in four years due to improved demand, raising hopes of wage restoration [2b47ff4fa01a, ff0f473e0921].
MANTRA-trained entrepreneurs have cumulatively scaled textile enterprises to ₹120 crore [7dc3005e0b28].
TEJAS Association, representing 35,000 loom machine owners, met and officially denied rumors of operational shutdowns [1a925ede03e9].
what_to_watch: Track cash-credit limit utilization and inventory aging among weaving and embroidery borrowers amid yarn price hikes and labor-induced downtime.
Monitor settlement timelines and potential spillover of the ₹62 crore weaver payment defaults to assess receivables health across fabric trade intermediaries.
Assess operational disruption from migrant labor shortages post-Diwali, specifically across embroidery and MMF weaving clusters.
